As the age of creation is over, I feel that Gods banding together to perform creations or actions might be a good thing. To perform a powerful action might require the power of many. It might make it more interesting too.

I do feel we should limit these councils in scope though. Perhaps a council should have a finite goal, like creating an army of darkness. When that action is completed, then the council dissolves. If a group of gods then wish to create a council of war, then they could form a new group. That way we don't end up with the same gods on the same side, continuously group voting.

We might also have a council lay out smaller objectives that it needs to complete. In order for it to complete the main objective. That way if a god, or gods, want to oppose the Counsil, they can thwart its actions to bring about its goal. However, once the smaller objectives are met, then the larger objective cannot be stopped. > for example, gathering the ingredients to cast a powerful spell. Or the events that lead to a war.

I think this could be fun way of achieving large events, and large story arcs. Without it descending into eternally opposed factions. I would also suggest that we put a limit on the number of gods that can join a council, so that opposing forces might remain equal

Please let me know what you think, thanks.
